facts.statement: The India International Bullion Exchange (IIBX) was launched by the Prime Minister on 29 July 2022 and is regulated under the IFSCA (Bullion Market) Regulations, 2025; IIBX's full form is India International Bullion Exchange and it is located in GIFT City, IFSC.
IIBX ecosystem participants: Trading Members, Clearing Members, Qualified Jewellers (QJs), Qualified Suppliers (QS/QS-LPTM), Vault Managers, Bullion Depositories and Clearing Corporations.

Qualified Jeweller eligibility: engaged in ITC(HS) codes 7106/7108/7113/7114/7118, GST returns filed, 90% average annual turnover in precious metals over the last 3 FYs certified by CA/CS/CMA, and minimum net worth of INR 25 crore - reduced to INR 15 crore by circular of 10 October 2025.

IIBX block deals require a minimum of 100 kg gold or 3,500 kg silver at a price within +/-0.5% of the market price; margin trading is permitted only on T+1 or T+2; a trading member needs at least 1 employee with 2 years' experience and a market-maker needs 3 years of precious-metals experience.

IIBX clearing norms: a bullion refinery needs tangible net worth of at least USD 7 million, 5 years' refining experience and annual production of at least 5 tonnes gold or 25 tonnes silver for the last 3 years; the Settlement Guarantee Fund is minimum USD 1 million or the stress-test value; clearing member net worth is at least USD 10 million with collateral of at least 50% of total assets in cash/gold/cash equivalents.

The IIBX default waterfall sequence: (1) defaulter's funds plus SGF contribution, (2) insurance, (3) clearing corporation resources equal to 5% of Minimum Required Capital, (4) penalties, (5) clearing corporation contribution of at least 12.5% of MRC.

IIBX operational rules: Bullion Depository Receipts are created within 2 hours; physical bar verification is fortnightly; audit trails are maintained for 10 years; vault managers register via Form A (First Schedule) with promoters having 3 years' vaulting business, USD 7 million net worth, and a net-worth certificate submitted within 45 days of the end of March and September.

RBI permits resident entities to hedge gold price risk on IIBX and India INX (circulars of February and April 2024), and Indian banks were permitted to participate from February 2024; DGFT's January 2022 notification enabled QJ imports through IIBX.

IIBX FY2024-25 volumes: gold 93.07 tonnes (USD 7.93 billion), silver 239.18 tonnes (USD 228.31 million); 167 Qualified Jewellers, 37 Qualified Suppliers and 441 TRQ holders (Mar-25), rising to 197 QJs and 45 QSs by Dec-2025; India's gold imports FY25 were 812.22 tonnes (USD 48.5 billion) and silver 7,669.40 tonnes (USD 3.39 billion).
facts.detail: CSJ-era baseline: over 16 tonnes gold imported via IIBX by June 2024 and 1,000+ tonnes silver; 3 vault managers with capacity 420 tonnes gold and 2,200 tonnes silver; 129 QJs notified mid-2024.

facts.statement: The 2 January 2026 bullion circular expanded IIBX import eligibility: SEZ units with valid Letter of Approval plus jewellery export as authorised operation, net worth of at least INR 5 crore and annual export turnover of at least INR 5 crore in ITC 7113 over the last 3 FYs; Advance Authorisation holders for specified purposes; general non-SEZ entities with net worth INR 15 crore; silver bars under ITC(HS) 71069221 exempt from Qualified Jeweller notification; half-yearly compliance monitoring with suspension under Clause 5A; aligned with India-UAE CEPA.
